title: Composition of relative-section logarithmic morphisms
statement: Let $X,Y,Z$ be arbitrary schemes [def-pc-scheme] with etale log structures $L,M,N$ and log morphisms $f:(X,L)\to(Y,M)$ and $g:(Y,M)\to(Z,N)$ in the relative-section sense of [def-trf-log-ideal-chart-presentation]. Define their composite as follows. Its underlying scheme morphism is $g\circ f$. For an etale object $W\to Z$, an etale object $V\to X$, and $k:V\to W$ with $W\to Z$ composed with $k$ equal to $V\to X\to Y\to Z$, form $U=Y\times_ZW$ [def-pc-fibre-product], an object of the small etale site of $Y$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Let $l:V\to U$ be the canonical map with components $V\to X\to Y$ and $k$. The composite relative section homomorphism is $N(W)\xrightarrow{g^\flat}M(U)\xrightarrow{f^\flat}L(V)$, using the second projection $U\to W$ and $l$. Retain the naturality and structural compatibility inherited from these section maps. This is the canonical construction on all relative etale diagrams, without an etaleness, strictness, fineness, saturation or Noetherian assumption on $f$ or $g$.
